source.title: On the integral Hodge conjecture for real varieties, I
source.version: Author-hosted published 77-page version with Inventiones pagination and DOI; not the 67-page revised preprint linked on Wittenberg's homepage.
readSections: Entire published article: introduction, §§1.1–1.6, §§2.1–2.4, §§3.1–3.6, §§4.1–4.3, §§5.1–5.4, acknowledgments and references; all proofs, pp.1–77.
Printed pp.55 and 59 visually inspected: dimension hypothesis of Theorem3.16 and complex conjugations in Example4.4.

Re-read on 22 September 2026 for this checkpoint: the whole of §1.2–1.3, §3.3–3.6 and the introduction, in the same author-hosted published PDF (sha256 daeb43ec…, re-downloaded and the hash re-checked), and in the LaTeX source of arXiv:1801.00872v3 (source archive sha256 25d11f433052792b396d274557d120f1fe0d1d3db4ba3d8f2d53168a64a01eb3, file partie_1.tex, 4856 lines), whose statement numbering differs from the published numbering but whose text agrees. The LaTeX was used for three mechanical audits, all clean: no duplicate \label, no undefined \ref, and no mismatch between the word before a cross-reference and the environment carrying that label.

Codex codex-c83e7a third checkpoint: independently read every published page 1–77, including proofs and references. Visually checked pp.19,34,37,43,44,48,55,59; checked Example4.4 against arXiv v3 partie_1.tex lines3973–4048. Page34 projection arrow is correctly oriented, not a source issue.

summary: Benoist–Wittenberg formulate the real integral Hodge conjecture in the equivariant cohomology of X(C) and, assuming it for 1-cycles, describe the algebraic classes on X(R), the existence of curves of even geometric genus and the image of torsion 1-cycles (Theorems A and C); for rationally connected or simply connected Calabi–Yau threefolds they reduce the conjecture to these conditions (Theorem B). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item (the four Questions added), every missing item is routed exactly once, and ten findings are recorded. Theorem A(ii)/3.16(ii) is false for curves with a real point (E1), the Example 4.4 construction is impossible (E3), and Remarks 5.10 are announced without proof (E10). Not formalised.
conventions: R denotes any real closed field, C=R(i), G=Gal(C/R)=C2; actual real numbers are written ℝ. A variety is separated of finite type; smooth/proper/geometrically irreducible are not implicit unless explicitly imposed by an item.
HG means Borel/sheaf equivariant semi-algebraic cohomology, not Bredon cohomology. Write M(j)=M⊗Z(j), Z(j)=i^jZ with the parity sign action. Ordinary singular comparison is asserted only over ℝ.
All sheaf and cycle constructions below are mathematical planning contracts, not completed formalizations. API tests are specified but not executed in Lean.

For §3 items, S3 denotes: X/R smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible, pure dimension d>0. For §5.4, S54 denotes S3, R=ℝ or H²(X,O_X)=0, real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles, and CH0(X_C') supported on a surface for EVERY algebraically closed extension C'/R.
Integral restriction coordinates α_p mean the parity-restricted components in (1.30) followed by mod-two reduction of the top integral component. Components outside range are zero; Sq^i=0 for i<0.
No conjecture named in the introduction or Questions2.1,2.6,2.16,4.9 is asserted as a theorem. Paper Part II results are external inputs, not proofs in Part I.

Example4.4 uses the natural lift g=f² with weights (1,7,2,6,3,5,0). T(Q)=conjugate(Q(f(x))) is conjugate-linear on polynomial coefficients; T²=g*. The displayed invariant complete intersection does not exist: see E3. This is not a claim that all real Campedelli surfaces are impossible.

items.name: Real closed field carrier
items.statement: A field R is real closed when it is semireal, exactly one of x and −x is a square for x≠0, and every odd-degree polynomial has a root; use the pinned IsRealClosed class rather than a new field carrier.
proofSteps: Read the actual class and ordered-field constructor.
items.note: This item is only the field carrier, not the algebraic-closure theorem for R(i).

items.name: Periodic finite cyclic group cohomology
items.statement: For a representation A of a finite cyclic group generated by g, H^0 is the invariant kernel; positive even cohomology is the homology of N→A→(g−1), and odd cohomology the homology of (g−1)→A→N, with N the cyclic norm.
proofSteps: Read the resolution and each parity isomorphism.
items.note: Specialized integral C2 products and equivariant sheaves still need adapters.

items.name: Shapiro isomorphism for representations
items.statement: For a commutative ring k, subgroup S≤G and k-linear S-representation A, H^n(G,Coind_S^G A)≅H^n(S,A) for every n≥0.
proofSteps: Read groupCohomology.coindIso and its projective-resolution construction.
items.note: This does not on its own prove the sheaf-equivariant geometric Shapiro comparison.

items.name: Pure Hodge structure carrier
items.statement: On a complex vector space with conjugation, a pure weight-n Hodge structure is an exhaustive decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to conjugate F^(n+1−p); reuse HodgeStructureOn and its integral base-change specialization.
proofSteps: Read the actual structure, not only its name.
items.note: No geometric Hodge decomposition, integral Hodge conjecture or cycle class is inferred from this carrier.

items.statement: For smooth pure-d-dimensional separated finite-type schemes over a field, the geometric finite-coefficient compact-support trace pairing and its proper specialization have complementary degree 2d and twist d, with derived integral versions retaining Ext terms.

items.name: Semi-algebraic real and complex loci
items.statement: For X/R finite type, form X(R) with its semi-algebraic site (semi-algebraic opens, admissible finite covers); obtain X(C) by gluing Weil restrictions of affine charts. Complex conjugation acts with fixed locus X(R).
proofSteps: Glue the Weil-restriction charts and use definable topology, imported from LD.6.

items.statement: For X/R a variety and a torsion G-module M, H^i_G(X(C),M) canonically identifies with H^i_et(X,M); for ℓ-adic coefficients the integral semialgebraic groups compare after completion under the finite-generation hypotheses used in §1.1.1.

items.name: Free-action descent and dimension bounds
items.statement: For a free semialgebraic G-action, equivariant cohomology equals cohomology of the quotient with the descended sheaf. items.name: Blowup decomposition of admissible classes
items.statement: For smooth X/R, smooth irreducible center Z of codimension r and blowup π:Xtilde→X with exceptional i:E→Xtilde, τ:E→Z and ξ=cl(O_E(1)), the map (α,(β_j))↦π*α+Σ_{j=k−r+1}^{k−1}i_*(ξ^{k−j−1}τ*β_j) is an isomorphism HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0⊕⊕_j HG^{2j}(Z(C),Z(j))_0≅HG^{2k}(Xtilde(C),Z(k))_0.
proofSteps: Apply the ordinary equivariant blowup decomposition; the forward direction follows from pullback, pushforward and product compatibility.
For the converse α=π_*γ is admissible. The corrected exceptional formula gives δ=−i*(γ−π*α), hence δ is admissible.
Induct upward on j from k−r+1 to k−1 using equation(2.5), τ_*ξ^(r−1)=1 and τ_*ξ^m=0 for m<r−1. Subtract previously admissible terms to recover β_j.

items.statement: For smooth affine X∈S_k and finitely many points t_i, a theory is strictly effaceable at them if for every neighborhood W, p≥0 and closed Z⊂W of codimension≥p+1, there are a neighborhood U⊂W of the t_i and closed Z'⊂W containing Z with codimension≥p such that h_Z∩U^q(U)→h_Z'∩U^q(U) is zero for every q.

items.name: Explicit form of the derived integral cup product
items.statement: In the diagram of the proof of Proposition1.7, the map H^{i-d}(X(R), τ_{>0}(e)) is given by x ↦ xγ̃ + β_{ℤ̃}(x)β_{ℤ̃}(γ̃), where γ̃ ∈ H^0 ⊕ H^2 ⊕ ··· is the unique class with γ = γ̃ + β_{ℤ̃}(γ̃). In particular the derived cup product with integral coefficients, read through the canonical twisted integral decomposition (1.29), is not the sum of the individual cup product maps, in contrast with ℤ/2ℤ coefficients, where it is, by (1.28).
items.locator: Remark1.9, on the diagram in the proof of Proposition1.7
proofSteps: The authors state the formula without proof and do not use it; it is recorded because it pins the difference between the integral and the mod-two decompositions of the derived cup product, which the rest of §1.2 relies on implicitly.

items.name: Euler-characteristic map does not factor through homological equivalence over general fields
items.statement: For X smooth and proper over an arbitrary field and i an integer, sending an integral dimension-i cycle to the Euler characteristic of its structure sheaf gives CH_i(X) → ℤ/elw_{i-1}(X)ℤ, which factors through algebraic equivalence (Kóllar, Proposition14). Over a real closed field and for i = 1 it factors even through homological equivalence, by Theorem3.6. This does not extend to arbitrary fields: let X be the smooth projective quadric threefold over ℂ((t))((u))((v)) defined by the anisotropic quadratic form ⟨1,t,u,tu,v⟩. Then H^4_ét(X,ℤ_2(2)) is torsion-free, while CH_1(X)_tors has order 2 and is generated by a class whose image in ℤ/elw_0(X)ℤ = ℤ/2ℤ does not vanish.
items.locator: Remark3.13; the quadric example rests on Karpenko, Theorem5.3 and Theorem3.8
proofSteps: Torsion-freeness of H^4_ét(X,ℤ_2(2)) is checked with the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.
The order and the generator of CH_1(X)_tors are quoted from Karpenko, Theorem5.3 and Theorem3.8; elw_0(X) = 2 because the quadratic form is anisotropic, so X has no rational point.
items.note: Named in the previous checkpoint's coverage block as still to extract. The published PDF text loses the third Laurent variable; the LaTeX source of arXiv:1801.00872v3 gives the field as ℂ((t))((u))((v)) and the form as ⟨1,t,u,tu,v⟩, five variables, which is what makes X a threefold. Whether the assertion holds for all i is stated as open.

items.name: Conjugate pullback on the quadratic equation space
items.statement: For the displayed f, define T(Q)(x)=conjugate(Q(f(x))). This is an invertible conjugate-linear operator on complex quadrics, T²=g*, and T sends weight r to weight−r. If a reduced projective subvariety Y is f-stable then T preserves its degree-two vanishing ideal.
items.locator: Example4.4, published p.59; extracting-worker proof in report
proofSteps: Polynomial substitution followed by conjugation removes conjugates of variables but conjugates scalar coefficients.
Apply the definition twice to get Q(f²(x)); use commutation of f and g, with conjugation of eigenvalues.
For y in Y, f(y) is in Y; hence T sends equations of Y to equations of Y. Invertibility gives equality.

items.name: The weight-four space has no conjugate-pullback-stable line
items.statement: On the basis (a,b,c,d)=(x0x4,x1x5,x2²,x3²), T(Aa+Bb+Cc+Dd)=conjugate(B)a−conjugate(A)b+conjugate(D)c−conjugate(C)d. Consequently T²=−id and no nonzero one-dimensional complex subspace of Λ_2 is T-stable.
items.locator: Example4.4, published p.59; extracting-worker proof in report
proofSteps: Compute the four basis images directly using ζ⁴=−1.

A stable line with generator Q≠0 would have TQ=uQ. Applying T gives −Q=conjugate(u)uQ, so |u|²=−1, contradicting nonnegativity. This argument applies to every complex scalar, not merely the finite diagnostic sample.

items.name: Four defining quadrics generate the quadratic vanishing space
items.statement: Let Q0,...,Q3 be four complex quadrics defining a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection surface Y in P⁶. Then H⁰(P⁶,I_Y(2)) is their four-dimensional complex span. In particular, if Qi has distinct g*-weight2i, its intersection with Λ_2 is exactly C Q2.
items.locator: Example4.4, published p.59; extracting-worker proof in report
proofSteps: The regular-section Koszul resolution of I_Y, twisted by2, is 0→O(−6)→O(−4)^4→O(−2)^6→O^4→I_Y(2)→0.
Projective-space cohomology vanishes in degrees1 through5; negative twists here also have no H⁰. Break into short exact sequences to obtain H⁰(I_Y(2))≅C⁴.
Smoothness makes the scheme reduced, so setwise f-stability preserves this ideal. Four distinct nonzero weight components give the stated one-dimensional intersection.
